keyVerseText: Then stood there up one in the council, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, and commanded to put the apostles forth a little space;
rootMeaning: The name Γαμαλιήλ (Gamaliel) originates from the Hebrew גַּמְלִיאֵל (Gamlîyʼêl), meaning "reward of God." This etymology highlights a deeply theological concept embedded in the name: a divine recompense or blessing. Beyond being a mere personal name, it carries the implication of one who is recognized or established by God's favor, which enriches the understanding of the character associated with this name in Scripture.
usageInScripture: The word Γαμαλιήλ appears twice in the New Testament, consistently translated as 'Gamaliel' or 'of Gamaliel,' indicating a proper noun referring to a specific individual. This limited but consistent usage underscores the importance of this figure as an Israelite Pharisee and a respected teacher of the law. The stable translation reflects the recognition of a historically significant person rather than a general concept or title.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding the name Gamaliel as 'reward of God' invites reflection on how God raises up leaders and teachers within His covenant people to guide and preserve the faith. Gamaliel's role as a Pharisee and doctor of the law places him within the tradition of rigorous adherence to God's commands, emphasizing the value of godly wisdom and reputation in the community. For the Christian faith, this reminds believers that God’s providence works through human agents, even those outside the immediate Christian circle, to fulfill His redemptive purposes. It also points to the importance of respecting those who diligently study and teach Scripture, as they can serve as instruments in God's plan.
keyVerseReflection: Acts 5:34 introduces Gamaliel as a Pharisee and doctor of the law who enjoys a good reputation among the people, highlighting his authority and influence. The use of his name here conveys not only his identity but also the weight of his counsel in the council. Recognizing Gamaliel as 'reward of God' enriches this passage, suggesting that his wise and measured intervention in defending the apostles is part of God's providential reward and preservation of His church.
